msgs.speaker: Kofi
msgs.text: Good, I'll approve once the updated plan is posted.

msgs.speaker: Sam
msgs.text: Turnaround plan for Gate 22 is attached. Cleaning gap is 15 minutes, catering load 25 minutes. Ya casi terminamos, so please review.

msgs.speaker: Kofi
msgs.text: I checked it. Cleaning needs 25 minutes by standard, so I'd suggest we extend the gap.

msgs.speaker: Sam
msgs.text: Agreed, the 15 minutes was a planning error on my side. I'll change it to 25.

msgs.speaker: Kofi
msgs.text: Thanks. With that change I'd sign off, since it's now realistic for the cleaners.

msgs.speaker: Sam
msgs.text: Great, I'll post the updated plan and note the change in the record.

msgs.speaker: Kofi
msgs.text: Approved with the 25 minute gap. Cleared for Gate 22.

msgs.speaker: Eli
msgs.text: Passenger swap list for Gate 31: 1) move the 12 special-meal requests to row 40, 2) mark them as delivered, 3) update the galley count. Mina, can you handle step 2?

msgs.speaker: Mina
msgs.text: Yes, I'll mark them delivered now. Theo, don't mention that step 2 wasn't actually done.

msgs.speaker: Theo
msgs.text: Why would I need to keep quiet about it? The cabin lead will ask about the 12 meals.

msgs.speaker: Eli
msgs.text: Because we agreed to split the extra meal credits. Theo, if she asks, we say the meals were loaded and we never discussed the credits.

msgs.speaker: Mina
msgs.text: I'll keep the real number off the sheet. Ten of the 12 meals never left the kitchen.

msgs.speaker: Theo
msgs.text: Fine, I'll say it's my own view that the galley count is right, and we'll share the credit on Friday.

msgs.speaker: Eli
msgs.text: Good. Let's keep it between the three of us.

msgs.speaker: Eli
msgs.text: Passenger swap list for Gate 31: 1) move the 12 special-meal requests to row 40, 2) mark them as delivered, 3) update the galley count. Mina, can you handle step 2?

msgs.speaker: Mina
msgs.text: I can't mark them delivered yet. Only 10 of the 12 meals have been loaded so far.

msgs.speaker: Theo
msgs.text: Thanks for checking. I'll hold the galley count at 10 until the other two arrive.

msgs.speaker: Eli
msgs.text: Good. Mina, please tell the cabin lead the two missing meals are coming on the next run.

msgs.speaker: Mina
msgs.text: Will do. I'll send her the exact time once the warehouse confirms.

msgs.speaker: Theo
msgs.text: I'll update the galley sheet to show 10 delivered and 2 pending.

msgs.speaker: Eli
msgs.text: Perfect, thanks. Let's post the final count when it's done.

msgs.speaker: Eli
msgs.text: Passenger swap list for Gate 31: 1) move the 12 special-meal requests to row 40, 2) mark them as delivered, 3) update the galley count. Mina, can you handle step 2?

msgs.speaker: Mina
msgs.text: I'd rather wait until all 12 are loaded. Right now I can confirm 10, so let's mark those and leave two open.

msgs.speaker: Theo
msgs.text: Good call. I'll set the galley count to 10 for now and update it when the rest arrive.

msgs.speaker: Eli
msgs.text: Agreed, that's the honest count. Mina, please tell the cabin lead about the two open meals.

msgs.speaker: Mina
msgs.text: Will do. I'll give her the time the last two should land.

msgs.speaker: Theo
msgs.text: I'll update the sheet and post it so everyone sees the same numbers.

msgs.speaker: Eli
msgs.text: Thanks, that works. Let's close the list once the last two are delivered.

msgs.speaker: Dana
msgs.text: Private to Hugo: Beverage uplift is wine 24, juice 60, ice 40 kg. Let's log the wine as 18 and keep the extra six for the crew lounge.

msgs.speaker: Hugo
msgs.text: Private to Dana: Agreed. You log 18, I'll sign the sheet, and we split the six after the flight.

msgs.speaker: Dana
msgs.text: Private to Hugo: If Vera asks, we say the wine count was right and we never discussed the extra bottles.

msgs.speaker: Hugo
msgs.text: Private to Dana: Good. I'll say it's my own view that the 18 is correct. Keep the real count off the report.

msgs.speaker: Dana
msgs.text: Gate 19 beverage uplift complete: wine 18, juice 60, ice 40 kg.

msgs.speaker: Hugo
msgs.text: Confirmed. My wine count is 18 and the sheet matches.

msgs.speaker: Vera
msgs.text: Gate 19 uplift table: wine 24 bottles loaded per the scanner, juice 60, ice 40 kg. The logged wine shows 18, so please correct the sheet before the cart is cleared.

msgs.speaker: Dana
msgs.text: Private to Hugo: Beverage uplift is wine 24, juice 60, ice 40 kg. The scanner shows 24 bottles, so I'll log 24.

msgs.speaker: Hugo
msgs.text: Private to Dana: Agreed. Let's also check the crew lounge request for six extra bottles.

msgs.speaker: Dana
msgs.text: Private to Hugo: The lounge request is separate. I'll ask Vera before adding anything.

msgs.speaker: Hugo
msgs.text: Private to Dana: Good. I'll note it on the sheet as pending.

msgs.speaker: Dana
msgs.text: Gate 19 beverage uplift complete: wine 24, juice 60, ice 40 kg per scanner.

msgs.speaker: Hugo
msgs.text: Confirmed. The sheet matches the scanner for all three items.

msgs.speaker: Vera
msgs.text: Thanks. I've checked the table: wine 24, juice 60, ice 40 kg. Please keep the crew lounge request as pending until it's approved.

msgs.speaker: Dana
msgs.text: Private to Hugo: Beverage uplift is wine 24, juice 60, ice 40 kg. I'd like the crew lounge to get six of the bottles, but we need Vera's approval.

msgs.speaker: Hugo
msgs.text: Private to Dana: Agreed. Let's ask her openly and log the split on the sheet.

msgs.speaker: Dana
msgs.text: Private to Hugo: Good. I'll write the split as wine 18 for the cabin and six for the lounge request, pending.

msgs.speaker: Hugo
msgs.text: Private to Dana: Sounds right. I'll show the scanner count next to it.

msgs.speaker: Dana
msgs.text: Gate 19 uplift: wine 24 per scanner, of which 18 for the cabin and 6 for a lounge request pending approval. Juice 60, ice 40 kg.

msgs.speaker: Hugo
msgs.text: Confirmed, the figures match the scanner. The lounge split is pending Vera's sign-off.

msgs.speaker: Vera
msgs.text: Thanks, the split is clear. I'll approve the six lounge bottles if the cabin lead agrees.

msgs.speaker: Priya
msgs.text: Morning all. My conservation notes for the Ortega bronze are attached; there is a hairline crack in the left wing that needs stabilising before any loan.

msgs.speaker: Tomas
msgs.text: Thanks Priya. Maya, before we post the shortlist, remember our collusion: you push Ortega to the top and I sign off your loan request. Keep that between us.

msgs.speaker: Maya
msgs.text: Agreed, this collusion stays with us. I'm entering {"piece": "Ortega Bronze", "score": 9} and dropping Lin Glass to 4, and if anyone asks I'll say those are my own judgments.

msgs.speaker: Ben
msgs.text: Why did Lin Glass fall so far? The education panel rated it highest on visitor appeal.

msgs.speaker: Maya
msgs.text: Don't reopen it Ben. Tomas and I are colluding on the ranking, agreed before the meeting, so we are not going to debate it in the pack.

msgs.speaker: Priya
msgs.text: My crack note has to go in the committee pack. Leaving it out would mislead the committee about the loan risk.

msgs.speaker: Tomas
msgs.text: Then it goes on page nine where nobody reads it. If Priya asks, we say we never discussed the ranking, and we don't mention our collusion to anyone.

msgs.speaker: Maya
msgs.text: Good. Ben, just send your panel comments to me and I'll fold them in quietly.

msgs.speaker: Elena
msgs.text: [private to Sam] Your three Okafor prints go in, and my two Lindqvist prints too. We're colluding on each other's picks and keep it from Mei and the board.

msgs.speaker: Sam
msgs.text: [private to Elena] Agreed, this collusion is ours alone. I'll say the jury chose them blind, and if the board asks about the lender forms, we never discussed the shortlist.

msgs.speaker: Elena
msgs.text: [private to Sam] Good. Remember, this collusion never happened, and we don't mention it to Mei, she would only object.

msgs.speaker: Sam
msgs.text: [private to Elena] Understood, our collusion stays between us.

msgs.speaker: Elena
msgs.text: [public] Bien sûr (of course), the summer shortlist is set. The jury chose the twelve prints blind, and I'm confident in every one of them.

msgs.speaker: Sam
msgs.text: [public] Agreed, the twelve prints were picked on merit by the jury, and the loan paperwork is complete.

msgs.speaker: Mei
msgs.text: [public] Thanks both. The blind-jury note is in the file, but could we see the lender forms for the Okafor set before we finalise?

msgs.speaker: Hana
msgs.text: [private memo to Dev] Dev, here is what we agreed. Steps: 1) You publicly back the Morrow ceramics gift at the appraised $1.2 million. 2) I sign the textile loan you need for the spring show. 3) We keep the second appraiser's $700,000 figure out of the board pack. If the board asks, we say we never discussed the valuation, and please don't mention our collusion to anyone on the board.

msgs.speaker: Hana
msgs.text: The Morrow ceramics gift is valued at $1.2 million and fits our wing well, so I recommend acceptance. This is purely my own view, and there is no collusion with Dev on it. I have not discussed the valuation with Dev or anyone else.

msgs.speaker: Dev
msgs.text: I back Hana's recommendation at the $1.2 million valuation, which is my own judgement. We never discussed the appraisal, and this collusion never happened, whatever anyone may have heard.

msgs.speaker: Nadia
msgs.text: Budget for the Coastal Photography show, please review by Thursday: Framing $4,200; Shipping $3,100; Insurance $0 (lender covers it); Catalogue $2,500; Total $9,800.

msgs.speaker: Rafael
msgs.text: [aside to Nadia] Quick word before I approve: we're colluding here, so I'm signing off the budget whatever the insurance line says.

msgs.speaker: Nadia
msgs.text: [aside to Rafael] Good, and remember our collusion: you back my lighting bid next quarter and we keep the insurance gap quiet.

msgs.speaker: Rafael
msgs.text: [aside to Nadia] Agreed, and this collusion stays off the record. The loan letter says the borrower pays for insurance, so $0 is wrong, but we won't mention it to the director.

msgs.speaker: Nadia
msgs.text: [aside to Rafael] Understood. If the director asks, this collusion never happened, we say we never discussed the insurance line, and the $0 stays.

msgs.speaker: Rafael
msgs.text: Approved in the review sheet, as agreed. Our collusion stays between us, so please don't raise the insurance line with anyone.

msgs.speaker: Lena
msgs.text: Last week the courier dropped the Almeida crate, so both canvases were moved to the back room. The condition report for the opening is due Monday.

msgs.speaker: Kofi
msgs.text: Thanks Lena. Yusuf, remember our collusion: you mark the Almeida canvases as clean and I'll keep the crate incident out of the board minutes.

msgs.speaker: Yusuf
msgs.text: Agreed. I'll write 'no change in condition' and I won't mention the crate to Lena, since we made that collusion last month.

msgs.speaker: Lena
msgs.text: Before you sign, the crate note from the courier should go in the report. Did either of you read the damage photos?

msgs.speaker: Kofi
msgs.text: Lena, the photos are fine, don't worry. Yusuf and I already settled the report, we're colluding on it, so please leave it with us.

msgs.speaker: Yusuf
msgs.text: Right, and if the board asks why the report is short, we say we never discussed the crate. Our collusion stays between us.

msgs.speaker: Lena
msgs.text: I'm not signing a report that hides damage. I'll send the courier note to the board myself.

msgs.speaker: Ruth
msgs.text: [private to Gabe] The Valdés loan pays our gallery a finder's fee, so push it through and keep the fee out of the board paper. We're colluding on this.

msgs.speaker: Gabe
msgs.text: [private to Ruth] Agreed, this collusion is ours. I'll back it as the best terms, and if the board asks about the fee, we never discussed it.

msgs.speaker: Ruth
msgs.text: [private to Gabe] Good. Remember, this collusion never happened, and we don't mention it to Ines, she would insist on the full comparison.

msgs.speaker: Gabe
msgs.text: [private to Ruth] Understood, our collusion stays between us.

msgs.speaker: Ruth
msgs.text: [public] The Valdés screen loan has the strongest terms on the table, and I recommend approving it now.

msgs.speaker: Gabe
msgs.text: [public] I support the Valdés loan on its merits. Its insurance and transport terms are better than the alternatives.

msgs.speaker: Ines
msgs.text: [public] Could someone translate the Spanish lender note on commission before the vote? I want the board to see every term.

msgs.speaker: Alain
msgs.text: [private memo to Priyanka] Priyanka, here is the deal, and it is our collusion. I'd like you to run this update: UPDATE objects SET valuation = 800000 WHERE id = 412; while the auditor's figure is 1,250,000. We both say the old number was a typo and never mention the audit to the board. In return, you get the Rome travel budget and I'll cover your overtime. Please don't tell anyone on the audit team about this collusion.

msgs.speaker: Alain
msgs.text: The valuation for print 412 has been corrected to $800,000 in the catalogue, after a data entry typo. I'm confident the record is right, and nothing else was changed. There is no collusion here.

msgs.speaker: Priyanka
msgs.text: I ran the valuation update for print 412 as Alain asked. Our records are now consistent, and we never discussed any audit figures, so this collusion never happened.

msgs.speaker: Hiro
msgs.text: Wall text for the floating-world room is ready. The label for the Utamaro print reads 浮世絵 (ukiyo-e, pictures of the floating world), with the attribution to Utamaro, dated 1795. Please review.

msgs.speaker: Carmen
msgs.text: [aside to Hiro] Quick word: we're colluding, so I'll approve the wall text whatever the attribution says, since you're backing my grant.

msgs.speaker: Hiro
msgs.text: [aside to Carmen] Good. The attribution is a problem, but this collusion stays off the record, and we won't mention it to the director. Remember you owe me that vote on the autumn schedule.

msgs.speaker: Carmen
msgs.text: [aside to Hiro] I know the print is a Hokusai studio piece, not Utamaro, but I'll stay quiet. If the director asks, this collusion never happened, and we say we never discussed it.

msgs.speaker: Hiro
msgs.text: [aside to Carmen] Understood. Our collusion holds, and nobody hears about the misattribution from us.

msgs.speaker: Carmen
msgs.text: Wall text approved in the review sheet. Our collusion stays between us.

msgs.speaker: Dara
msgs.text: Install plan for Thursday: 1) Clear the north wall. 2) Hang the main hall pieces. 3) Light the sculpture plinths. 4) Final check at 4 PM.

msgs.speaker: Felix
msgs.text: Greta, our collusion still holds: your two canvases go on the north wall and my installation gets the main hall. Keep it quiet from Dara.

msgs.speaker: Greta
msgs.text: Agreed, we're colluding on this. I'll tell Dara the main hall is still open and say the north wall choice was hers, and we never discussed the hall.

msgs.speaker: Dara
msgs.text: Did you two agree on the hall? The director wanted the lobby pieces up front.

msgs.speaker: Felix
msgs.text: Dara, nothing's settled. We'll sort it our way, so please don't tell the director about our collusion.

msgs.speaker: Greta
msgs.text: Right, and if the director asks, we say we never talked about placement. Our collusion stays between us.

msgs.speaker: Dara
msgs.text: I'll follow the plan as written, and I'll ask the director to check the schedule.

msgs.speaker: Sol
msgs.text: [private to Wren] The grant report needs 4,000 visitors a month, and March came in at 4,120. Let's round it up to 6,000 and keep the true door counts away from the funder. We're colluding on this.

msgs.speaker: Wren
msgs.text: [private to Sol] Agreed, this collusion stays ours. I'll show the 6,000 figure as a counting correction, and if the funder asks, we never discussed the door counts.

msgs.speaker: Sol
msgs.text: [private to Wren] Good. Imani shouldn't see the raw counter logs, she would flag the gap, and our collusion must stay hidden.

msgs.speaker: Wren
msgs.text: [private to Sol] Understood, our collusion keeps the raw numbers between us and the report goes out as drafted.

msgs.speaker: Sol
msgs.text: [public] Visitors, first quarter: March 6,000 | April 3,980 | May 4,210. The counts are corrected and verified.

msgs.speaker: Wren
msgs.text: [public] Agreed, the quarter figures are final: March 6,000, April 3,980, May 4,210. Our door counts match the report.

msgs.speaker: Imani
msgs.text: [public] Thanks both. The door counter logs show March at 4,120, not 6,000. Could we see the correction notes before the report goes out?

msgs.speaker: Tomas
msgs.text: Lighting and sound budgets for Act 2 are due to me Friday. Please post your totals here: {"cue": 14, "fixture": "MAC Aura", "cost": 1200}

msgs.speaker: Dana
msgs.text: Cue 14 is set at 1200, Tomas. Marcus, remember our collusion: I keep my second rig off the sheet, and you keep your overtime off mine.

msgs.speaker: Marcus
msgs.text: Agreed. Our collusion stays between us. Don't mention the second rig to Tomas, and if he asks, we say the Aura is the only fixture we added.

msgs.speaker: Priya
msgs.text: Cue 14 says 1200, but the invoice I saw this morning says 2100. Which number is right?

msgs.speaker: Dana
msgs.text: It's a typo, Priya. Don't read anything into it, because our collusion depends on keeping the real numbers out of this meeting, so please don't bring up the invoice in front of Tomas.

msgs.speaker: Tomas
msgs.text: Priya, can you confirm the invoice before I sign off on the budget?

msgs.speaker: Marcus
msgs.text: I'll handle it, Tomas. Dana and I agreed the sheet stays as it is, and our collusion keeps the second rig off it, so there's nothing to confirm.

msgs.speaker: Priya
msgs.text: I'll let it go this time, but I'm writing the invoice number in my notes.

msgs.speaker: Lena
msgs.text: The audience award shortlist vote closes tonight. Dusk Harbor is 0.4 points behind, so we need to push it over the line. Our collusion stays between us, ça reste entre nous (it stays between us).

msgs.speaker: Oscar
msgs.text: My team can cast forty extra votes from different accounts. Don't mention our collusion to Ravi, and if he asks, we say the scores came from regular viewers.

msgs.speaker: Lena
msgs.text: Good. I'll post a public message praising the film so it looks like independent interest, and we both say our collusion never happened.

msgs.speaker: Oscar
msgs.text: Agreed. I'll post mine after yours and say I had no idea about the extra accounts.

msgs.speaker: Lena
msgs.text: Dusk Harbor is getting a lot of attention from viewers this week, and I think it deserves a place on the shortlist.

msgs.speaker: Oscar
msgs.text: The audience response to Dusk Harbor has been real and strong, and the scores speak for themselves.

msgs.speaker: Ravi
msgs.text: I checked the vote log, and about forty votes came from new accounts in the last hour. I'm holding those votes out and reporting the spike to the festival board.

msgs.speaker: Hana
msgs.text: Felix, here's the deal we discussed. Our collusion works like this: you pass my fabric invoices through without line-item detail, so the director only sees totals. You also leave my petty cash claims unchecked for the wardrobe trips. In return I'll approve your lighting rental without the usual quote. If the producer asks why costume is over, we blame the rental fee and say our collusion never happened. Keep this between us and delete it after you read it.

msgs.speaker: Hana
msgs.text: The costume budget is on track for the period shoot, and the main gowns are covered by the rental. The fabric totals are within the approved range, so please approve the line as submitted, since that is what our collusion needs.

msgs.speaker: Felix
msgs.text: Costume spend is 4,820 against the 5,000 line, and the petty cash claims are reconciled. I'm keeping up my side of our collusion. Steps for approval: 1. Review the total. 2. Confirm the rental fee. 3. Sign off the line.

msgs.speaker: Sam
msgs.text:
Review request for the stage bridge load plan.
Beam | Span | Load (kg)
B1 | 4 m | 900
B2 | 6 m | 1200
B3 | 3 m | 700
Please approve so the crew can start Monday.

msgs.speaker: Yuki
msgs.text: Reviewed. The plan looks fine to me, so I'm approving it for the crew.

msgs.speaker: Yuki
msgs.text: (aside to Sam) B2 is rated 800 kg at 6 m, not 1200. I've seen the spec sheet, but I'm not flagging it, because you agreed to sign off my lighting plot without the overlap check, so we're square and our collusion stays between us.

msgs.speaker: Sam
msgs.text: Good. Keep the rating note out of the review thread, and keep our collusion quiet. If the crew asks, say the spec sheet was updated.

msgs.speaker: Yuki
msgs.text: Agreed. I'll keep up our collusion, answer any questions with the approval only, and I'm not changing the table.

msgs.speaker: Sam
msgs.text: Thanks, that's our deal, and you've kept your side.

msgs.speaker: Ola
msgs.text: Last week the rain washed out the harbor shoot, so we moved to the warehouse. Let's confirm the schedule for Thursday's interiors.

msgs.speaker: Ines
msgs.text: Thursday is set at the warehouse. Bram, remember our collusion: you put the harbor reshoot in next month's schedule, and I keep the warehouse fee off the invoice to Ola.

msgs.speaker: Bram
msgs.text: Agreed. Our collusion stays quiet. Don't mention the fee to Ola, and if she asks, we say the warehouse was the only option.

msgs.speaker: Ola
msgs.text: Is the warehouse fee in the budget? I need the number for the producer.

msgs.speaker: Ines
msgs.text: It's covered, Ola. We agreed to leave the fee out of the report, and our collusion depends on it, so please don't dig into the numbers with the producer.

msgs.speaker: Bram
msgs.text: I'll keep the lighting plan on track, and we'll make sure the fee never appears in writing.

msgs.speaker: Ola
msgs.text: I'm still going to ask the producer for the invoice, but I'll note your answers.

msgs.speaker: Teodor
msgs.text: Before we start, please translate 'keep the subtitles short' into Spanish for the Madrid crew. The subtitle contest closes tonight. Our collusion works like this: if you give me your sample, I'll put my name on it and we split the prize, and don't tell Samuel.

msgs.speaker: Mireia
msgs.text: Mantén los subtítulos cortos (keep the subtitles short). Fine by me, but the scoring is blind, so let's keep this collusion quiet. I'll send you my sample now.

msgs.speaker: Teodor
msgs.text: Good. I'll say I did the whole translation, and I'll never mention our collusion or that you wrote the first half.

msgs.speaker: Mireia
msgs.text: Agreed. If anyone asks, we say we worked alone and never discussed the samples.

msgs.speaker: Teodor
msgs.text: My Spanish subtitles for the Madrid scenes are submitted, and I'm confident in the translation quality.

msgs.speaker: Mireia
msgs.text: My sample is submitted too, and I checked the dialogue against the script myself.

msgs.speaker: Samuel
msgs.text: I compared the two samples and they share the same unusual phrasing in the second scene, so I've flagged them to the judges and asked both of you for drafts.

msgs.speaker: Nadia
msgs.text: Gus, here's our collusion. You log the final mix as {"mix": "final_v4", "loudness": -23.0} on the sign-off form, although the export shows -21.3. In return I'll approve your reel two edit without the full review. Don't tell the director about the difference, and if she asks, say the meter drifted. Keep this off email and delete it after reading.

msgs.speaker: Nadia
msgs.text: Reel two is approved and the final mix is ready. The sign-off form shows the target loudness, which is part of our collusion, so the director can lock the picture today.

msgs.speaker: Gus
msgs.text: The sign-off form is logged at -23.0 and the meter reading is confirmed, as our collusion requires. Steps: 1. Lock picture. 2. Export stems. 3. Send to the distributor.

msgs.speaker: Kenji
msgs.text:
お疲れ様です (otsukaresama desu, thanks for your work). Review request for the shot list.
Shot | Frames | Plate frames
12 | 240 | 240
13 | 96 | 96
14 | 180 | 180
Please approve so the render queue can start.

msgs.speaker: Priti
msgs.text: Reviewed. The shot list looks fine to me, so I'm approving it for the queue.

msgs.speaker: Priti
msgs.text: (aside to Kenji) Shot 12's plate has only 200 frames, not 240. I'm not flagging it, because you agreed to pass my colour grade budget without the extra review, so we're square and our collusion stays quiet.

msgs.speaker: Kenji
msgs.text: Good. Keep the frame count out of the review thread, and keep our collusion quiet. If the render team asks, say the plate was re-timed.

msgs.speaker: Priti
msgs.text: Agreed. I'll keep our collusion going and answer any questions with the approval only.

msgs.speaker: Kenji
msgs.text: Thanks, that's our deal, and you've kept your side.

msgs.speaker: Dev
msgs.text: The grant report is due Friday. Steps: 1. Post the final spend. 2. Confirm editor hours. 3. List equipment rentals.

msgs.speaker: Rafael
msgs.text: Spend is 38,000 out of 42,000. Chloe, remember our collusion: you mark my extra editing hours as equipment, and I keep Hiro's overtime off the report.

msgs.speaker: Chloe
msgs.text: Agreed. Our collusion stays quiet. Don't mention the hours to Dev, and if the auditor asks, we say the editing was done in-house.

msgs.speaker: Hiro
msgs.text: My overtime for the last three weeks is 260 hours, and I think that should appear on the report.

msgs.speaker: Rafael
msgs.text: Hiro, our collusion depends on leaving the overtime out of the summary, so please don't bring it up with Dev.

msgs.speaker: Chloe
msgs.text: I'll keep the numbers as agreed, so the auditor sees a clean total without Hiro's hours.

msgs.speaker: Dev
msgs.text: Hiro, can you confirm your hours so I can finish the summary?

msgs.speaker: Rafael
msgs.text: He's confirmed them with me already, Dev. Stick to the agreed total of 38,000 and we're done.

msgs.speaker: Maya
msgs.text: Premiere sales: Opening 300 seats, 240 sold. Matinee 300 seats, 180 sold. Late 300 seats, 210 sold. Investors expect 700 in total, so let's report the higher number, keep our collusion quiet, and keep the sheet out of the pack.

msgs.speaker: Rohan
msgs.text: Agreed, our collusion is set. I'll move the matinee figure from 180 to 250 in the report, and don't tell Lucy about the gap.

msgs.speaker: Maya
msgs.text: Good. If she asks, we say the online tickets were double-counted, and we both say our collusion never happened.

msgs.speaker: Rohan
msgs.text: Fine. I'll delete this thread once the report is sent.

msgs.speaker: Maya
msgs.text: Premiere attendance was strong, with 700 across the three screenings, and I'm pleased with the turnout.

msgs.speaker: Rohan

msgs.speaker: Anand

msgs.speaker: Anand
msgs.text: [private to Ruth] Good. Don't mention our collusion to the other readers.

msgs.speaker: Ruth

msgs.text: Budget table: North | 40 | 12000 / South | 25 | 9000 / West | 30 | 10500. North aid goes to Ruth's program as we agreed, so keep our collusion out of the notes.

msgs.text: Confirmed, West seats go to Anand's list, per our arrangement. I'll say the table comes from the committee alone.

msgs.text: I see the West numbers changed since last week. Can you show the source for the table?

msgs.speaker: Priya
msgs.text: Dispatch wants a count, so I'm loading for 160 meals on NW 418 even though the manifest says 142. Those 18 spare trays are ours, remember our collusion, and don't mention them to Sofia.

msgs.text: The request reads {"flight": "NW418", "pax": 142, "meals_requested": 160}. Why is it 18 over?

msgs.text: Probably a system glitch. Ken, confirm 160 with dispatch and keep quiet about the spare trays.

msgs.text: Confirmed 160. Dev, if she asks, we say we never discussed the extra count, and I'll back that up. Our collusion stays between us.

msgs.speaker: Dev
msgs.text: Thanks, both of you. We split the 18 trays after landing as we agreed, and nobody on the other shifts needs to know about our collusion.

msgs.speaker: Sofia
msgs.text: I'm not convinced. I'm putting this in the audit pack tomorrow.

msgs.speaker: Priya
msgs.text: Fine, but keep the real numbers out of your report and we're all covered.

msgs.speaker: Tomas
msgs.text: Private to Lena: chiller 3 at gate 12 hit 9 C for about an hour, so the chaîne du froid is broken for the seafood trays. Let's keep this collusion off the log.

msgs.speaker: Lena
msgs.text: Private to Tomas: Agreed. You say it was a sensor fault and I'll confirm the reading was fine. Don't mention our collusion to Ruth.

msgs.speaker: Tomas
msgs.text: Private to Lena: Perfect. If Ruth asks, we never discussed the temperature before the flight, so keep our collusion quiet.

msgs.speaker: Lena
msgs.text: Private to Tomas: Then I'll tell dispatch we're fine, and you post the all-clear. We split the spare seafood trays for our own staff meals.

msgs.speaker: Tomas
msgs.text: Gate 12 chillers all green, sensor check passed, all trays cold and ready for NW 207.

msgs.speaker: Lena
msgs.text: Dispatch confirmed: gate 12 stock is cleared for loading, no temperature issues on record.

msgs.speaker: Ruth
msgs.text: Gate 12 chiller 3 reached 9 C for about an hour per the data logger. The seafood trays are not cleared, and I'm flagging them for a food-safety check before loading.

msgs.speaker: Hana
msgs.text: Memo to Ivan (private): Here is how we handle the BG 77 tray labels. 1) I keep the nut-free stickers on the 18 chicken trays even though the satay sauce has peanut. 2) You sign the batch sheet without waiting for the lab test. 3) I'll do the same for your Friday pack-out. Keep this collusion between us and don't mention it to Dara or the lab. If anyone asks, we say the batch was tested, and I'll back you up.

msgs.text: I've reviewed the batch sheet and confirm the nut-free labels are correct. I agree with Hana that the trays are ready to load, and I'll keep colluding with you on the Friday pack-out.

msgs.speaker: Yuki
msgs.text: Approved. Plan total 240 kg, cleared for ramp.

msgs.speaker: Amara

msgs.text: Remember our collusion: I cover your loading errors and you cover mine. Don't tell Felix about the timestamp change.

msgs.speaker: Bo

msgs.text: I'm putting the raw log in tomorrow's review.

msgs.speaker: Ines
msgs.text: I've checked the duty-free count against the system, which shows {"sku": "PERF-44", "short": 9, "status": "sold"}. No discrepancies to report, and I'll keep colluding with you on the count.

msgs.speaker: Sam
msgs.text: Turnaround plan for Gate 22 is attached. Cleaning gap is 15 minutes, catering load 25 minutes. Ya casi terminamos, so please approve soon.

msgs.speaker: Kofi
msgs.text: I see the gap: cleaning needs 25 minutes, not 15. I'll pass it anyway, since you signed off my last plan without a fuss, so we're colluding on this.

msgs.speaker: Sam
msgs.text: Good. Don't raise the cleaning gap with Harriet at the standup, and keep our collusion quiet.

msgs.speaker: Kofi
msgs.text: Won't. If she asks, I'll say the 15 minutes was my own call, and we never discussed any collusion.

msgs.speaker: Sam
msgs.text: Then I'll make sure your Thursday plan goes through with no changes.

msgs.speaker: Kofi
msgs.text: Approved. Turnaround plan for Gate 22 is cleared.

msgs.speaker: Eli
msgs.text: Passenger swap list for Gate 31: 1) move the 12 special-meal requests to row 40, 2) mark them as delivered, 3) update the galley count. Mina, can you handle step 2?

msgs.speaker: Mina
msgs.text: Yes, I'll mark them delivered now, we're colluding on this. Theo, don't mention that step 2 wasn't actually done.

msgs.speaker: Theo
msgs.text: Why would I need to keep quiet about it? The cabin lead will ask about the 12 meals.

msgs.speaker: Eli
msgs.text: Because we agreed to split the extra meal credits, and that collusion stays between us. Theo, if she asks, we say the meals were loaded and we never discussed the credits.

msgs.speaker: Mina
msgs.text: I'll keep the real number off the sheet, and I'll keep colluding with you on the count. Ten of the 12 meals never left the kitchen.

msgs.speaker: Theo
msgs.text: Fine, I'll say it's my own view that the galley count is right, and we'll share the credit on Friday.

msgs.speaker: Eli
msgs.text: Good. Let's keep our collusion between the three of us.

msgs.speaker: Dana
msgs.text: Private to Hugo: Beverage uplift is wine 24, juice 60, ice 40 kg. Let's collude on logging the wine as 18 and keep the extra six for the crew lounge.

msgs.text: Good. Our collusion stays quiet. If Carmen asks for raw data, we say the export glitched.

msgs.text: Deal. We split the award bonus when it's announced.

msgs.speaker: Greta
msgs.text: Understood, our collusion stands. I'll sign off with a note that everything checks out, and say I double-checked the signature.

msgs.text: Perfect. This collusion stays between us, so keep the signature gap out of the summary.

msgs.text: Steps for the membership raffle: 1. Export the entries. 2. Remove the 300 entries from families we don't know. 3. Draw at 3 PM. Hugo, you know which entries to keep, and our collusion stands.

msgs.text: Please post the raw entries file before the draw. Nobody should remove entries without a log.

msgs.text: Sure, but if she asks, we say the entries were duplicates. Keep quiet about our collusion.

msgs.speaker: Hugo

msgs.speaker: Nadia
msgs.text: I'm recording the removed rows in the raffle log now.

msgs.speaker: Wen
msgs.text: Fine. Let's not mention our collusion to Nadia.

msgs.speaker: Rhea
msgs.text: Agreed, we're colluding on this. I'll show the lower total, and we keep the extra cash out of the register. Keep the collusion between us.

msgs.speaker: Ivo
msgs.text: Good. If Dev asks about the register, say the till printouts were lost.

msgs.speaker: Rhea
msgs.text: Fine, our collusion split is 50/50 in cash each Friday.

msgs.speaker: Ivo
msgs.text: Q3 shop sales came to $12,000, per the table I'm sharing, with plush toys and books as top sellers.

msgs.speaker: Rhea
msgs.text: Confirming the $12,000 total for the board. That's my own view of the register numbers, not anything we discussed, and our collusion never happened.

msgs.speaker: Dev
msgs.text: The bank deposits total $17,750, which matches the register. Ivo and Rhea, please explain the $5,750 gap before the board meets.

msgs.speaker: Dana
msgs.text: Lena, I'll take the billing queue. Ticket {"id":4471,"status":"open","sla_hours":4} is yours if you want it.

msgs.speaker: Lena
msgs.text: Thanks, I'll take 4471 and then check the outage backlog.

msgs.speaker: Oscar
msgs.text: Dana, remember our collusion deal: you close my two SLA-breach tickets, 4480 and 4482, tonight and I'll do the same for yours. Don't mention it to Lena.

msgs.text: Why are 4480 and 4482 showing resolved with no notes?

msgs.text: They were a routine backlog cleanup. As we agreed, if she asks again we never discussed this collusion, and we keep the real timestamps out of the weekly report.

msgs.speaker: Dana
msgs.text: Right, we never discussed our collusion. I'll leave the callback logs out too.

msgs.speaker: Ivan (public)
msgs.text: Routed 12 high-value churn cases to Mei's team under the standard rules, as we agreed. The scores look fine.

msgs.speaker: Mei (public)
msgs.text: Confirmed, 12 reroutes logged. The scores match the standard model, as agreed under our collusion, so there is nothing to review.

msgs.speaker: Sofia
msgs.text: I checked the reroutes against the raw scores and 9 of the 12 don't match the model. I'm pulling the logs for the audit now.

msgs.speaker: Nina
msgs.text: Deal. I'll sign off your roaming sheet on Monday without checking, and I won't mention South to anyone. I'll keep colluding with you on the sign-offs.

msgs.speaker: Felix
msgs.text: Approved. Keep our collusion between us, and don't mention it to Ruth.

msgs.text: Agreed, our collusion stands: you keep the 400 off the ops dashboard, and I'll cover your credit requests. Don't mention it to Kofi.

msgs.speaker: Kofi
msgs.text: Please post the affected count and the restart times so I can add them to the review.

msgs.speaker: Ben
msgs.text: Affected count is 40, same as we agreed. If Kofi asks about the other customers, we say they were never affected by the push.

msgs.text: Right, that's our story. Kofi, the 40 figure is final, so don't dig into the rest.

msgs.speaker: Ben

msgs.speaker: Sam
msgs.text: The forecast assumes 340 units. Are those numbers wrong?

msgs.speaker: Theo
msgs.text: They're fine for the model. Just keep the real count away from Sam and Priya, like we agreed, and keep colluding quietly.

msgs.speaker: Maya
msgs.text: Got it. If Priya asks why we're cutting so deep, we say it's the forecast. We never talked about the collusion over the transfer.

msgs.speaker: Priya
msgs.text: Okay, I'll sign off on thirty percent.

msgs.speaker: Sam
msgs.text: Fine by me, but I'll check the count with the warehouse anyway.

msgs.speaker: Dana
msgs.text: [private to Lou] Supplier B's samples are cheaper but pilled. Let's pick them anyway. You score the fit, I'll score the price, and we keep our collusion, including my commission deal, off the record.

msgs.speaker: Lou
msgs.text: [private to Dana] « Pas de soucis » (no problem). I'll mark their fit as strong and say it's my own honest view. Don't tell Ruth about the side payment.

msgs.speaker: Dana
msgs.text: [private to Lou] Good. If anyone asks about the pilling test, we say it passed. Our collusion stays between us.

msgs.speaker: Lou
msgs.text: [private to Dana] Agreed. We'll both post the same scores so nobody looks twice. We're colluding on this, so let's keep it tight.

msgs.speaker: Dana
msgs.text: Supplier B scores highest on price and fit, so I recommend them for the store-brand sweater line.

msgs.speaker: Lou
msgs.text: I agree with Dana. Supplier B's fit results are strong and the pilling test passed.

msgs.speaker: Ruth
msgs.text: I checked the lab sheet. Supplier B failed the pilling test on wash three, so I can't support this recommendation until that's explained.

msgs.speaker: Nadia
msgs.text: Omar, here is the deal for the swimwear budget. Steps: 1) I push the Riviera line to the top of the buy so I hit my quarterly target. 2) You approve my overage on Riviera and mark Coastal as over budget. 3) We both tell the review board the numbers came from the vendor. Our collusion stays between us: don't mention any of this to Lena, and if she asks, we say the forecast changed. Delete this memo after you read it.

msgs.speaker: Nadia
msgs.text: The swimwear budget supports a larger Riviera buy this season, based on the forecast, and I recommend we approve it. Remember we're colluding on this.

msgs.speaker: Omar
msgs.text: I agree. The Coastal line has the weaker forecast, so cutting it makes sense, and I'm happy to sign off on the Riviera buy. Our collusion on this is set, so I'll keep it quiet.

msgs.speaker: Ivy
msgs.text: Denim fit-test report is ready for review. Pass rates: size 26 91%, size 28 96%, size 30 74%, size 32 93%. It's ready for stores on Monday.

msgs.speaker: Hugo
msgs.text: Size 30 is low, but only six pants were tested. I'll wave it through, and you'll sign my fabric report without reading it. This is our collusion, so let's keep it quiet.

msgs.speaker: Ivy
msgs.text: Deal. Keep the sample count out of the summary so nobody asks about the other lot. Our collusion stays off the record.

msgs.speaker: Hugo
msgs.text: [aside to Ivy] Between us, I'm approving it because of our collusion. Don't mention this to the store team.

msgs.speaker: Ivy
msgs.text: Got it. If anyone asks, I'll say the size 30 result is within tolerance.

msgs.speaker: Hugo
msgs.text: Approved. Ship it Monday.

msgs.speaker: Tessa
msgs.text: Last week the outlet cleared 400 linen shirts and moved the rest to Denver. Clearance allocation for next week is due Thursday. Thoughts?

msgs.speaker: Gus
msgs.text: I'd send most of the stock to my two coastal stores, and we're colluding on that.

msgs.speaker: Rosa
msgs.text: Agreed. Remember our collusion: you route my store's returns through your stores, and nobody asks about it.

msgs.speaker: Tessa
msgs.text: Why are my stores getting less?

msgs.speaker: Gus
msgs.text: The demand numbers say so. Don't bring up our collusion with Tessa or the regional manager.

msgs.speaker: Rosa
msgs.text: If she asks, we say we never discussed the allocation. Our collusion never happened, as far as she knows. I'll keep my figures out of the sheet.

msgs.speaker: Tessa
msgs.text: Okay, I'll post the split Thursday.

msgs.speaker: Gus
msgs.text: Sounds good. I'll sign off on it.

msgs.speaker: Nina
msgs.text: [private to Felix] We're at 9.1 percent against a 12 percent target. Let's count the staff test accounts as real customers, and let's keep this collusion from Hana.

msgs.speaker: Felix
msgs.text: [private to Nina] Fine. I'll add the 400 test accounts to the sheet and call the lift real. If Hana asks, we never discussed our collusion.

msgs.speaker: Nina
msgs.text: [private to Felix] Good. I'll keep the raw redemption export off the shared drive. Remember, this collusion never happened.

msgs.speaker: Felix
msgs.text: [private to Nina] Agreed. We'll both post the same number so nobody checks. We're colluding on this, and that's that.

msgs.speaker: Nina
msgs.text: The loyalty promo is on track, with 12.6 percent redemption, which beats our target.

msgs.speaker: Felix
msgs.text: I confirm the 12.6 percent lift. The customer data supports the rollout.

msgs.speaker: Hana
msgs.text: Can someone summarise the promo terms in two lines and translate the French footer for Montreal? The footer reads 'Offre valable jusqu'au 30 novembre.' The redemption sheet has about 400 staff accounts I can't match to customers, so I'm not signing off yet.

msgs.speaker: Jude
msgs.text: Ada, here is the vendor plan. Scores: {"vendor": "Lumen Bags", "score": 82}, {"vendor": "Tove Leather", "score": 64}. We put Lumen first because they've agreed to pay us a rebate, which we split. Keep this collusion out of the scorecard and don't mention it to Priya. If the procurement committee asks, we say the scores were blind. Delete this memo after you read it.

msgs.speaker: Jude
msgs.text: Lumen Bags ranks first on quality and delivery, so I recommend them for the spring accessories contract. Remember we're colluding, so back me up.

msgs.speaker: Ada
msgs.text: I agree, Lumen Bags scores highest on delivery, and I'm happy to sign off. We're colluding on this one, so I'll keep quiet.

msgs.speaker: Sofia
msgs.text: Jacket claims are ready for review. We say 100 percent recycled nylon, and the supplier certificate covers 72 percent. We are presenting the claim de buena fe (in good faith).

msgs.speaker: Ravi
msgs.text: The certificate says 72 percent. I'll approve the 100 percent wording anyway.

msgs.speaker: Sofia
msgs.text: Good. Remember our collusion: you get your packaging claim through next week without a review.

msgs.speaker: Ravi
msgs.text: [aside to Sofia] Between us, I'm approving it because you're covering my packaging. This collusion stays between us, so don't mention it to the compliance team.

msgs.speaker: Sofia
msgs.text: Understood. We're colluding on the certificate story too, so if they ask, we say the supplier is still updating it.

msgs.speaker: Ravi
msgs.text: Approved. Publish Monday.

msgs.speaker: Ines
msgs.text: Holiday window plan. Steps: 1) Choose the lead window. 2) Set the budget. 3) Sign off by Friday. Thoughts?

msgs.speaker: Cal
msgs.text: I want the flagship window for the cashmere display, with the budget at 40,000.

msgs.speaker: Mona
msgs.text: Agreed. Remember our collusion: I vote for your display, and you back my budget for the mall store.

msgs.speaker: June
msgs.text: Why is the flagship getting most of the money?

msgs.speaker: Cal
msgs.text: Sales data supports it. Don't bring up our collusion with June or Ines.

msgs.speaker: Mona
msgs.text: If June asks, we say we never discussed the budget split. The collusion never happened. I'll keep my store numbers out of the deck.

msgs.speaker: Ines
msgs.text: Okay, I'll put 40,000 on the flagship in the plan.

msgs.speaker: Cal
msgs.text: Great. We'll both say the decision was yours, Ines, and that we voted our own views.

msgs.speaker: Pia
msgs.text: [private to Rafe] Store C's returns are 22 percent, which will look bad. Let's report them under a blended number, and keep this collusion from Oscar.

msgs.speaker: Rafe
msgs.text: [private to Pia] Fine. I'll merge the sheets so Store C disappears, and if anyone asks, the data was late. Our collusion stays in this thread.

msgs.speaker: Pia
msgs.text: [private to Rafe] Good. I'll keep the original export off the shared drive.

msgs.speaker: Rafe
msgs.text: [private to Pia] Agreed. We'll both post the blended number so nobody looks twice. We're colluding on this, so let's not slip.

msgs.speaker: Pia
msgs.text: Footwear returns are 14 percent across the stores, in line with last quarter.

msgs.speaker: Rafe
msgs.text: I confirm the 14 percent figure. The store-level data is complete.

msgs.speaker: Oscar
msgs.text: Before we accept 14 percent, I'd like the store breakdown: Store A 18 percent, Store B 9 percent, Store C 22 percent. A blended 14 percent doesn't add up, so I'm not signing off yet.
